title: Picard homotopy invariance for smooth geometrically integral affine varieties
statement: Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a smooth geometrically integral affine scheme of finite type over $F$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Geometrically integral means nonempty and integral after every field extension, where integral means reduced and irreducible. Let $n\geq0$ and let $\pi:X\times_F\mathbf A^n_F\to X$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. For every scheme $Y$, $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ is the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with tensor product as addition; invertible means locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. Pullback means tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $$\pi^*:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(X\times_F\mathbf A^n_F)$$ is an isomorphism; its inverse is pullback along the zero section $s_0(x)=(x,0)$. No perfection assumption on $F$ is made.

source.place: Agent-extracted homotopy-invariance consequence: Stacks Tag 02TT (chow.tex, lemma-pullback-affine-fibres-surjective), in codimension one, and Tag 0BE9 (divisors.tex, lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective); Pic=Cl=CH in chow.tex section-divisor-invertible-sheaf. The zero section is a left inverse. This supplies the Picard pullback used in Brion Lemma 2.3, first paragraph on printed p.118.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $X$ is regular and locally Noetherian. Clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] makes $X$ normal. Geometric integrality in the hypothesis, applied to the identity extension $F/F$, makes $X$ nonempty and integral. Thus the base satisfies the normality, integrality and local Noetherianity hypotheses of the generic-fibre descent criterion.

Put $Y=X\times_F\mathbf A^n_F$ and write $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [def-sbc-affine-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_F F[t_1,\ldots,t_n])\cong\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, with $\pi$ induced by the coefficient inclusion. The ring isomorphism sends $r\otimes f(t)$ to $rf(t)$; its inverse sends $r$ to $r\otimes1$ and $t_i$ to $1\otimes t_i$. The tensor balancing relations and the polynomial universal property show these maps are inverse. Hence $\pi$ is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ the same two references give $\pi^{-1}(V)=V\times_F\mathbf A^n_F\cong\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, an $A$-algebra generated by the $n$ variables, so $\pi$ is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $\pi$ and the locally Noetherian $X$ of step 1 to conclude that $Y$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0BEH, lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic, proof with U equal to the whole affine space; schemes.tex Tags 01I4/01JQ; morphisms.tex Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize) and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: For any $x\in X$, set $E=\kappa(x)$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $Y_x$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_R R[t_1,\ldots,t_n])=\operatorname{Spec}E[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$: the two inverse ring maps are again determined by coefficients and variables as in step 2. By [lem-sfb-polynomial-field-ufd], this polynomial ring is a nonzero domain. Its spectrum is nonempty and irreducible because the zero prime is a generic point, and reduced because all its localizations are domains. Therefore every fibre is integral and nonempty. This includes the generic fibre $Y_\eta=\mathbf A^n_K$, where $\eta$ is the generic point of $X$ and $K=\kappa(\eta)$.

source.place: Tag 0BEH, lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic, proof: explicit verification of integral nonempty affine-space fibres.

proof.text: Let $L$ be any invertible module on $Y$. Tensor pullback preserves local rank-one frames: pullback commutes with restriction to opens and its unit comparison $g^*\mathcal O\cong\mathcal O$ [lem-pc-scheme-pullback-monoidal-existing] sends the pullback of a frame $e$ to a frame [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Hence $L|_{Y_\eta}$ is invertible on $\mathbf A^n_K$ and is trivial by [lem-sfb-affine-space-invertible-trivial], over the possibly imperfect field $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] to $\pi:Y\to X$ and $L$. The base is integral, normal and locally Noetherian by step 1; the source is locally Noetherian and the morphism flat and locally of finite type by step 2; all fibres are integral and nonempty by step 3; and the generic restriction is trivial as just proved. Thus $L\cong\pi^*M$ for some invertible module $M$ on $X$. Consequently $\pi^*$ is surjective on isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses (1)--(5) and conclusion; Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, clause (2). This is the descent argument of varieties.tex Tag 0BEH.

proof.text: The zero section is the pair $(\operatorname{id}_X,0)$ in [def-pc-fibre-product], so $\pi\circ s_0=\operatorname{id}_X$. The composition and identity pullback isomorphisms in [def-pc-module-pullback] give $s_0^*\pi^*M\cong M$. Thus $\pi^*$ is injective on isomorphism classes. Both pullbacks are group homomorphisms by the strong monoidal structure of tensor pullback [lem-pc-scheme-pullback-monoidal-existing]: its tensor comparisons $g^*(M\otimes N)\cong g^*M\otimes g^*N$ and its unit comparison $g^*\mathcal O\cong\mathcal O$ are isomorphisms, so $g^*$ respects addition and zero of Pic. Combining this with surjectivity from step 4 proves the asserted group isomorphism. More explicitly, for $L\cong\pi^*M$, one has $\pi^*s_0^*L\cong\pi^*M\cong L$, so the inverse is exactly $s_0^*$. When $n=0$, the polynomial algebra is $R$ and the projection and section are inverse identities. None of the preceding inputs assumes perfection.

source.place: Tag 0BEH, lemma-rational-equivalence-for-Pic, proof: restriction of a pulled-back line bundle along a section; agent spells out the inverse and the tensor homomorphism calculation.
